facts.statement: The genus Baurusuchus was first described by Price in 1945.
facts.quote: authority: Price, 1945

facts.statement: Baurusuchus lived in Brazil between 90 and 83.5 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: lived in Brazil from 90 to 83.5 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous period

facts.statement: Baurusuchus is estimated to have weighed up to 113.4 kilograms.
facts.quote: estimated to reach up to 113.4 kg in weight

facts.statement: B. salgadoensis had a bite force between 2542 and 3088 Newtons, which is considerable for its size.
facts.quote: produce a considerably strong bite force for its size (between 2542–3088 Newtons in B. salgadoensis)

facts.statement: The bite force of B. salgadoensis is comparable to that of the American alligator.
facts.quote: being comparable to that of the american alligator

facts.statement: Enlarged and strongly bent pterygoids allowed Baurusuchus to close its jaw very quickly using powerful muscles.
facts.quote: The enlarged and strongly bent pterygoids allowed for attachment of powerful muscles that could close its jaw very quickly

facts.statement: Baurusuchus likely hunted by ambushing prey and pulling back with serrated, blade-like teeth, similar to a Komodo dragon.
facts.quote: The skull and tooth morphology indicates that the biting strategies of Baurusuchus were similar to a Komodo dragon which include ambushing the prey, biting it and pulling back the serrated, blade-like teeth

facts.statement: Baurusuchus may have shaken prey violently with its jaws, aided by enlarged cervical neural spines that served as muscle attachments.
facts.quote: Perhaps violently shaking prey with its jaws like modern crocodiles, helped by its enlarged cervical neural spines, which served as large muscle attachments

facts.statement: Fossils of B. salgadoensis were found in sandstones interpreted as floodplains in a hot and arid climate.
facts.quote: B. salgadoensis was found in fine massive sandstones which are interpreted as a floodplain area in a hot and arid climate

facts.statement: Baurusuchus likely dug holes to find water during dry seasons or for thermoregulation, similar to modern alligators.
facts.quote: Baurusuchus was likely able to dig holes for finding water in dry seasons or, like modern alligators do, for thermoregulation

facts.statement: Baurusuchus likely competed with abelisaurid dinosaurs for food in its ecosystem.
facts.quote: Baurusuchus likely played an important role in its ecosystem, competing with the abelisaurids for food

facts.statement: Baurusuchus is the type genus of the family Baurusuchidae.
facts.quote: Baurusuchus is the type genus of the family Baurusuchidae

facts.statement: A 2011 study established a new subfamily called Baurusuchinae.
facts.quote: A study in 2011 erected a new subfamily called Baurusuchinae

facts.statement: Some researchers do not support the affiliation of B. albertoi to Baurusuchus, viewing it instead as a close relative of Aplestosuchus.
facts.quote: The species B. albertoi is an exception. The paper does not support its affiliation to Baurusuchus and views it as a close relative of Aplestosuchus

facts.statement: Baurusuchus was a terrestrial carnivore measuring between 3.5 and 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Era un carnívoro terrestre, de entre 3.5 a 4 metros de largo

facts.statement: The species B. pachecoi was named by Price in 1945.
facts.quote: B. pachechoi (Price, 1945)

facts.statement: The species B. salgadoensis was named by Carvalho et al. in 2005.
facts.quote: B. salgadoensis (Carvalho et al., 2005)

facts.statement: The species B. albertoi was named by Nascimento and Zaher in 2010.
facts.quote: B. albertoi (Nascimento & Zaher, 2010)

facts.statement: Baurusuchus belongs to the family Baurusuchidae.
facts.quote: familia: Baurusuchidae

facts.statement: The authority for the genus Baurusuchus is Price, 1945.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Price, 1945

facts.statement: B. salgadoensis is considered a terrestrial predator that lived in a hot and arid climate.
facts.quote: B. salgadoensis es considerado como un depredador terrestre, que vivía en un clima cálido y árido

facts.statement: The external nostril position was not adapted for an amphibious lifestyle like modern crocodilians, and the snout and teeth were laterally compressed like in theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: La posición de las narinas externas no estaba adaptada a la vida anfibia como los crocodilianos modernos y el hocico y los dientes estaban comprimidos lateralmente como en los dinosaurios terópodos

facts.statement: The highly curved pterygoid suggests a rapid bite, although this bite was somewhat weak.
facts.quote: El pterigoideo sumamente curvado sugiere una mordida rápida, aunque esta era algo débil

facts.statement: Baurusuchus had elongated cervical neural spines that functioned as large muscle anchors.
facts.quote: ayudados de espinas neurales cervicales alargadas que funcionan como grandes anclajes musculares

facts.statement: Baurusuchus is the type genus of the family Baurusuchidae, which includes crocodiliforms with elongated and laterally compressed skulls.
facts.quote: Baurusuchus es el género tipo de la familia Baurusuchidae, que abarca a crocodiliformes con cráneos alargados y comprimidos lateralmente.

facts.statement: A new subfamily called Baurusuchinae was established in a 2011 study.
facts.quote: Un estudio publicado en 2011 erigió a una nueva subfamilia llamada Baurusuchinae.

facts.statement: The subfamily Baurusuchinae includes only Stratiotosuchus and Baurusuchus, making Stratiotosuchus the closest known relative of Baurusuchus.
facts.quote: La subfamilia solo incluye a Stratiotosuchus y a Baurusuchus, lo que hace a Stratiotosuchus el pariente más cercano conocido de Baurusuchus.

facts.statement: A 2014 study referred a new species, Aplestosuchus sordidus, to the subfamily but supported a closer relationship between Baurusuchus and Stratiotosuchus than with Aplestosuchus.
facts.quote: No obstante, un estudio publicado en 2014 refirió a una nueva especie llamada Aplestosuchus sordidus a la subfamilia, pero apoyando una relación más cercana de Baurususchus con Stratiotosuchus que con Aplestosuchus.

facts.statement: The species B. albertoi is an exception, as a study does not support its affiliation with Baurusuchus and considers it a close relative of Aplestosuchus instead.
facts.quote: La especie B. albertoi es una excepción. El artículo no apoya su afiliación con Baurusuchus y lo considera como un pariente cercano de Aplestosuchus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Baurusuchus is Baurusuchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Baurusuchinae

facts.statement: Baurusuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Baurusuchus is Baurusuchus pachecoi.
facts.quote: Type species: Baurusuchus pachecoi

facts.statement: Baurusuchus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: While other family members are known from the Cretaceous of South America, baurusuchids are also known from the Cretaceous of Asia (Pakistan) and possibly the Tertiary of Europe.
facts.quote: Otros miembros de la familia del Cretácico de América del Sur incluyen a Stratiotosuchus y a Cynodontosuchus, aunque los baurusúquidos también son conocidos del Cretácico de Asia (Pakistán) y tal vez el Terciario de Europa.
